answer: Drift-Locked Behavioral Fingerprint. Each epoch, an identity's action graph must match its own prior-epoch statistics within a tolerance band, scored against a shared beacon of epoch timing. A clone farm cannot reuse one behavioral parameter set without splitting it, since consistent patterns form a crystal that sybils must fracture across identities. Attacker cost: N identities require N distinct stable behavior distributions, sustained across epochs, plus synchronization loss in the ocean of cross-epoch variance.
